request.summary: Create a fictional three-floor civic-building touch directory as a reusable signage schematic.
request.audience: Visitors using a shared landscape lobby kiosk to find public departments, rooms, and services.
request.primaryGoal: Let a visitor search or tap a destination and follow a reviewed step-free route across the redesigned public circulation and aligned floor transitions.

assumptions: The reusable example is a fictional canonical schematic and makes no fidelity claim about a real building.
The reusable example owns a fictional Level 1 main-lobby kiosk anchor. A customer deployment must replace and confirm that anchor against the installed screen.
Image generation supplies visual direction only; map geometry, floor relationships, and interaction anchors come from the architectural source and explicit semantic artifacts.

Because the public corridors are redesigned as explicit walkable surfaces, the reusable example includes a separately authored walkable mask and reviewed multi-floor route graph. These claims do not transfer automatically to a customer building.
The accepted surfaces are 1920x1080 and 1366x768 landscape touch displays.

surfaceStrategy.rationale: The information architecture is designed for landscape lobby kiosks; portrait placements require a separate composition.

ownership.rationale: Operators quick-edit public names, alternate-language labels, descriptions, categories, floor, hours, status, and keywords.
Geometry and route eligibility remain reviewed build artifacts and cannot be created by mutable table rows.
Operators configure public copy, initial floor, evidenced guidance strength, language behavior, and idle reset.
Coordinated presets remain safe while Custom exposes a complete semantic palette.
Search, selection, viewport, and floor inspection are private to the active kiosk session.

views.purpose: Browse, filter, search, or tap a destination.
Inspect one simplified floor with quiet interactive department zones.
Show destination information, reviewed distance and walking time, and cross-floor elevator guidance.
Provide an app-owned multilingual touch keyboard for search.

inputs.action: Select a department zone or control map pan and zoom.
Search, filter, select, change floors, and reset.
Filter destination names through the app-owned English and Spanish layouts.
Type in search and activate focused controls.

session.expectation: Selection, search, floor, and viewport reset after the configured idle interval or explicit reset.

rendering.rationale: The map preserves its authored coordinate system while the directory reallocates width across the accepted landscape surfaces.

motion.rationale: Short floor fades and marker pulses communicate focus; Off preserves every state without animation.

media.fallback: Show a designed map-unavailable state while keeping the directory usable.
media.rationale: The simplified three-floor SVG works offline and keeps geometry synchronized with interaction anchors.

branding.provenance: A civic floor-plan reference and generated visual studies establish the municipal directory language; committed geometry, copy, and branding remain fictional.
branding.fallback: Use a restrained neutral civic identity and the configured semantic theme.

states.expectation: Level 1, the persistent current-location marker, floor controls, and directory fill the Full-HD kiosk.
The same touch workflow remains usable at 1366x768.
Level 2 redraw and destinations render without changing the visitor-controlled zoom.
Level 3 redraw reflects the revised department zoning.
A same-floor destination draws the reviewed centerline route and shows its distance and walking time.
The reviewed route and markers remain registered to map coordinates after manual zoom without changing the selected viewport.
A cross-floor destination draws the reviewed path to the elevator, preserves the current viewport, and offers an explicit floor-change action.
After an explicit floor change, the continuation route begins at the aligned elevator and ends at the selected destination entrance.
A selected zone and target marker pulse without rendering a walking path.
The touch keyboard fits without covering search results or the close action.
The complete custom palette applies to interface, floor controls, map, and spotlight.
A long title remains complete at the readable floor.
Long destination names wrap without clipped glyphs or broken touch targets.
Long selected names remain complete in the detail panel.
A bound empty table shows a stable designed state instead of bundled rows.
A direct row array normalizes to the same directory.
A live table update replaces public metadata without changing locked map geometry.

behaviors.expectation: Selecting any destination preserves zoom, pan, and the currently inspected floor until the visitor explicitly changes them.
A same-floor destination renders only the reviewed graph centerline, with distance and walking time derived from the route result.
A destination on another level renders the reviewed route to the elevator, identifies the required transition, and exposes an explicit view-floor action without moving the viewport automatically.
The Level 1 kiosk marker remains visible and pulsing at rest and after selection when Level 1 is visible.
The selected map zone and target marker pulse when motion is enabled and remain static but visible when motion is Off.
The configured timeout clears selection, query, category, viewport, and floor state.
The app-owned keyboard enters English and Spanish search text and can be dismissed without losing the query.
Floor tabs switch among all three levels and retain a clear selected-floor state.
Pointer drag, wheel, and pinch gestures move and zoom the map without accidentally selecting a destination.
A live destination table update replaces public copy without rebuilding geometry.

visualDirection.summary: Translate dense architectural sheets into a calm, high-contrast civic directory with faithful floor proportions, white circulation space, softly colored department zones, and direct touch affordances.
signatureChoices: Three aligned floor diagrams use the same coordinate language so vertical transitions remain understandable.
Department zones are the touch targets; no decorative numbered circles clutter the maps.

visualReview.intent: A credible municipal lobby directory where visitors understand the building hierarchy immediately and can inspect any floor without losing spatial context.
focus: Verify all three floor redraws preserve the authoritative footprint, public spine, zone adjacency, and elevator/stair relationships.
Verify destination zones remain readable and selectable without marker clutter.
Verify same-floor routes remain inside the designed public corridor and cross-floor routes stop at the aligned elevator before continuing on the selected level.
Verify destination selection never moves the viewport automatically and the explicit floor action is obvious.
Verify long names, touch keyboard, map labels, current marker, target pulse, and all themes remain coherent without clipping.
